alex_w: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector rollout (v2.3.7) I'm seeing OOM spikes on a subset of hosts. Symptoms: sudden workspace growth during batched decode, KV prefill gets big and decode path fails. Repro in canary with low qps.

perf-bot: CI perf-run:serving/runtime: trunk v2.3.6 -> v2.3.7: +18% p99 latency, +9% mem pressure on 16GB GPUs (artifact: https://ci/redwood/1234) :warning:

maya_k: thx. Could you paste a short perf trace and one core dump? quick hypothesis: new kernel picks a slower path that holds larger temporaries (workspace resizing). also prefill is inflating KV because we keep full attention caches for the longer kernels.

alex_w: paste logs below — this is from a failing request (truncated):
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] request id=7f8a decode start seq=1024 batch=4
alloc workspace 1.3GB -> 2.8GB
kv_prefill: reserved 1.6GB
decode: OOM while allocating 512MB slab
trace: kernel=matmul_optim_v2 path=wide_heads->fallback_slow
```

maya_k: thanks. Two immediate knobs: 1) per-request workspace cap (cap workspace growth to X% of GPU free) 2) limit KV-prefill budget per-request (prefill_cap) so single requests can't hoard. Also we should record kernel-chosen metadata in traces.

jon_p: agree. I prototyped a soft-per-request cap last week — it throttles prefill if workspace usage > 60% of module budget. Patch: 
```
if (workspace_usage + requested > soft_cap) {
  prefill_budget = min(prefill_budget, prefill_budget * 0.5);
  route_to_streaming_prefill();
}
```

jon_p: that reduced worst-case OOMs in local tests. Also consider changing slab allocator free-list coalescing frequency — fragmentation spikes when many mid-size slabs are allocated by the new kernel. Running compaction every N allocations helped in my sim.

alex_w: any numbers from your sim?

jon_p: baseline (no cap): 12 OOMs / 10k requests. with soft_cap + compaction: 0 OOMs / 10k, p99 latency +4% but mean unchanged.

maya_k: good. Two more notes: kernel selection seems to prefer matmul_optim_v2 for seq>512 because of FLOP efficiency. But that path allocates a temp buffer for packed weights ~1.2x larger. We need kernel metadata so routing can choose memory-friendlier kernels for tight-memory hosts.

sophie: can we canary a config change instead of full rollback? e.g., enable soft-cap and prefill halving on 10% of traffic and target older host pools first. Ops can do 10% route.

alex_w: sounds sensible. I'll prepare a quick canary: reduce prefill_cap from 64MB->32MB and enable soft_cap 60% on canary fleet. Also add trace tag `kernel_choice` and `prefill_budget` so we can correlate.

perf-bot: Benchmark summary (local microbench):
- baseline (v2.3.6) p99 mem 11.2GB
- v2.3.7 w/o caps p99 mem 12.4GB (+1.2GB)
- v2.3.7 + soft_cap + halved prefill p99 mem 11.6GB
- impact on p99 latency: +3% for soft_cap config, +0.6% for halved prefill.

maya_k: can you also dump KV-cache fragmentation stats (slab occupancy, free runs distribution) for the canary? Preferably 1-min bins. If fragmentation climbs, we'll need to increase coalescing frequency or use segregated pools for prefill vs decode.

alex_w: will add metrics: `kv_frag_pct`, `slab_coalesce_runs`, `prefill_vs_decode_kb`. Plan: rollout script -> canary config -> 1h monitor -> revert/expand.

sophie: pinging infra for canary route. @ops_team please allocate 8 machines in canary pool with older hw labels.

jon_p: one last suggestion: add a fallback policy in router to choose kernel variant by host memory headroom. e.g., prefer matmul_compat (lower mem) at < 2GB free. tiny diff: `router.policy = host_mem > 2GB ? fastest : low_mem_friendly`

alex_w: thanks all. Action items:
- alex_w: push canary config (prefill_cap 32MB, soft_cap 60%) + add trace tags (ETA 2h)
- maya_k: prepare fragmentation dashboards and kernel metadata plumbing (ETA EOD)
- jon_p: land soft_cap algorithm in runtime gasketing (small PR)
- sophie: coordinate canary route with ops

alex_w: I'll post results in this thread after 1h. :thumbsup:
